detailedExplanation:
### Deep Technical Dive: JavaScript V8 Engine & Execution Lifecycle for Internal Engine Execution & Microtask Synchronization of Array.prototype.includes() & SameValueZero Search Semantics

1. **V8 Compilation Pipeline**: Modern V8 parses source text into an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). The **Ignition** bytecode interpreter produces compact bytecode, while **TurboFan** JIT compiler optimizes hot code paths into machine assembly.
2. **Execution Context & Scoping**: When code runs, the engine creates an Execution Context containing a Lexical Environment (let/const bindings in TDZ until evaluated) and a Variable Environment (var declarations hoisted). Closures capture parent lexical scopes in the memory heap.
3. **Event Loop & Microtask Priority**: Synchronous code executes on the single-threaded Call Stack. Microtasks (Promise resolutions, queueMicrotask) run immediately when the call stack empties, preceding macrotasks (setTimeout, DOM events) in the Event Loop cycle.
why:
Why does Internal Engine Execution & Microtask Synchronization of Array.prototype.includes() & SameValueZero Search Semantics exist in modern JavaScript?
1. Eliminates error-prone legacy patterns (callback hell, global scope pollution, hoisting bugs).
2. Enhances developer ergonomics with declarative, expressive, and self-documenting syntax.
3. Enables V8 and other modern engines to apply runtime JIT optimizations and efficient garbage collection.

followUpAnswers: Microtasks (Promise.then, queueMicrotask) have higher priority and run completely to exhaustion after every call stack frame, whereas Macrotasks (setTimeout, setInterval) run one per event loop tick.
V8 uses a Generational Garbage Collector (Scavenger for young generation, Mark-Sweep-Compact for old generation) tracing reachability from roots (window/global).
The TDZ is the period between entering scope and variable declaration evaluation; accessing let/const during TDZ throws a ReferenceError to prevent accessing uninitialized state.
